# SDK Parity Matrix

What each of the 7 Erghi SDKs actually implements right now, verified against real source code
(not READMEs, not assumptions), and when it was last checked. Regenerated by
`scripts/generate-parity-matrix.mjs` from `*/parity.json` in this repo plus
`docs/parity/swift.json` (a manually-synced reference copy, since Swift lives in
[`erghi-sdk-swift`](https://github.com/ErghiPlatform/erghi-sdk-swift), a separate repo).

Regenerated on: 2026-09-03

## Maintenance tier

- 🟢 **active** — gets build effort ahead of parity as the platform's API grows.
- 🟡 **maintenance** — real, working, tested code that keeps getting bug fixes and security
  patches, but is not proactively built ahead of parity. This is a founder-level decision per
  SDK (see `tier_reason` below), not something any agent should flip on its own.

| SDK | Tier | Last verified | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| JavaScript / TypeScript | 🟢 active | 2026-09-03 | Canonical HTTP+realtime client. Every other SDK either wraps this one (react) or ports its wire contract (dotnet/python/flutter/angular). |
| React | 🟡 maintenance | 2026-09-03 | Founder decision 2026-09-03: deprioritized alongside angular. Neither Chatwoot nor Intercom -- the closest comparable competitors at Erghi's stage -- maintain framework wrappers around their vanilla widget. Kept as real, working, tested code; not getting further active build investment. Bug fixes and security issues still land. |
| Angular | 🟡 maintenance | 2026-09-03 | Founder decision 2026-09-03: deprioritized alongside react. Neither Chatwoot nor Intercom -- the closest comparable competitors at Erghi's stage -- maintain framework wrappers around their vanilla widget. Kept as real, working, tested code; not getting further active build investment. Bug fixes and security issues still land. |
| Widget (Vanilla JS, embeddable) | 🟢 active | 2026-09-03 | The product's actual customer-facing embed. Not a wrapper -- this is the surface Chatwoot/Intercom-style comparisons are against, so it stays fully invested regardless of the react/angular call. |
| .NET / C# | 🟢 active | 2026-09-03 | Independent full client, richest single surface of any SDK today (attachments, conversation assignment, widget CRUD). |
| Python | 🟢 active | 2026-09-03 | Full independent client, near-1:1 parity with javascript on auth+chat. |
| Flutter / Dart | 🟢 active | 2026-09-03 | Real independent client for a platform with no wrapper alternative (no vanilla-widget equivalent exists for native mobile) -- unlike react/angular this SDK is not redundant with anything, so it stays actively invested even though it currently has the widest gaps of the 5 'core' SDKs. |
| Swift | 🟢 active | 2026-09-03 | Real independent client, no wrapper alternative for native Apple platforms. |

### Realtime

| SDK | Realtime | Protocol |
|---|---|---|
| JavaScript / TypeScript | ✅ | signalr-hub-over-websocket |
| React | ✅ | signalr-hub-over-websocket (delegates to @erghi-ai/sdk's client.connect()) |
| Angular | ✅ | signalr-hub-over-websocket (own implementation, angular/src/lib/services/signalr.service.ts, not shared with javascript) |
| Widget (Vanilla JS, embeddable) | ✅ | own visitor-token realtime layer, see widget/src/realtime.ts |
| .NET / C# | ✅ | signalr-hub-over-websocket (Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Client, native) |
| Python | ✅ | signalr-hub-over-websocket |
| Flutter / Dart | ✅ | signalr-hub-over-websocket |
| Swift | ✅ | signalr-hub-over-websocket, hand-rolled negotiate handshake over Starscream WebSocket (no native Swift SignalR client exists) |

### Platform-wide gaps (not per-SDK drift)

- **RAG**: supported by **zero** SDKs today — No RAG resource client anywhere in this SDK. Platform has one (Erghi/Erghi.Conversation/Api/Controllers/RagController.cs) that no SDK wraps yet -- this is a platform-wide gap, not JS-specific drift.
- **WEBHOOKS**: supported by **zero** SDKs today — No customer-facing outbound webhook registration API exists on the platform yet (only inbound provider webhooks like Telegram). Nothing to wrap.

## How to keep this honest

1. When the platform API changes, update the affected SDK(s)' `parity.json` in the same PR —
   flip the capability flag, add `evidence` (a `file:line`), bump `last_verified_against_api`.
2. `.github/workflows/parity-check.yml` regenerates this file in CI and fails the build if the
   committed version has drifted from what `*/parity.json` says — this file cannot go silently
   stale relative to the manifests it's generated from.
3. The manifests themselves *can* go stale relative to the real code — nothing automatically
   diffs them against `erghi-conversation-api`/`erghi-gateway-api`/`erghi-ai-service` yet. Treat
   `last_verified_against_api` as a trust signal: a manifest older than a few weeks deserves a
   re-read before you rely on it, the same way any other doc in this workspace does.
4. Swift (`docs/parity/swift.json`) is the one manifest this repo's CI cannot verify at all,
   because the code it describes lives in a different repo. Whoever changes
   `erghi-sdk-swift`'s capability surface is responsible for updating this copy too.

Per-package detail, evidence, and freeform notes live in each `parity.json` — this file is a
skimmable summary, not the full record.
